name: Sleep Disturbances
summary: Difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or maintaining a consistent sleep-wake cycle — affecting a large majority of autistic children and often worsening daytime behavior when unaddressed.
triggers: Differences in melatonin production affecting the sleep-wake cycle
Sensory sensitivities to light, sound, or bedding/clothing texture at night
Co-occurring anxiety or difficulty 'switching off' racing thoughts
Inconsistent bedtime routines or irregular schedules
Screen use or stimulating activity close to bedtime

remedies.text: Consistent, predictable bedtime routine with a visual schedule of the steps (bath, pajamas, book, lights out)
Melatonin supplementation, discussed with a pediatrician first, which has evidence for reducing time to fall asleep though less effect on night waking
Reduce sensory disruptors in the bedroom: blackout curtains, weighted blankets, white noise, tagless/soft pajamas
Limit screens and stimulating activity in the hour before bed

sources.label: Autism Speaks - ATN/AIR-P Strategies to Improve Sleep in Children with Autism
